anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet, the heater indicator is drawn as LED D2 with a 22 µF capacitor C14 on the HEATER net; no series current-limiting resistor is shown in that position.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the heater indicator is a status LED D2 with a series resistor R3 on the HEATER net, so the LED current must be limited by a resistor rather than a capacitor.

evidence.quote: A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net, so the heater output doubles as a visual "heater on" indicator at the board level
Microcontroller sheet: D2 LED and C14 22uF shown on the HEATER net near J5

anomalies.impact: If C14 is in series with D2, the LED will not conduct DC and the heater-on indication will be dead; if C14 is in parallel, the LED has no current limit and may be overdriven. Either way the intended visual heater indicator does not function as specified.

parsed.summary: The schematic largely matches the specified architecture, but the heater status indicator on the Microcontroller sheet is built with LED D2 and a 22 µF capacitor C14 instead of the specified D2 plus series resistor R3, so the heater-on visual indicator is not implemented as intended.
